title: Nebraska ace Jordy Frahm joins Huskers’ coaching staff after WCWS run
content:
Nebraska softball star Jordy Frahm, who completed her accomplished career last weekend at the Women’s College World Series, will become an assistant coach for the Huskers next season, the school announced Friday.

Frahm, an ace pitcher/power hitter, won her second NFCA Player of the Year Award this season, and won a pair of national championships at Oklahoma before transferring to her home-state school in 2023. In her final season, she led Nebraska to its first Women’s College World Series in 13 years, leaving Oklahoma City, where the Huskers won their first game before losing to Alabama and eventual national champion Texas.

It’s been an eventful week for Frahm, 23, who also announced on Monday that she and her husband, Trey, a Nebraska baseball player, are expecting a baby in December.

“I am beyond excited to join the Nebraska softball coaching staff,” Frahm said in a statement. “Playing softball for the Huskers was an incredible blessing to me and the coaches had a huge impact on me as an athlete and as a person.

“We are thrilled to have Jordy join our coaching staff,” said longtime Nebraska coach Rhonda Revelle. “She has had such an impact on Nebraska Softball as a player, and now she can continue giving back to this program and being instrumental in the growth and development of our student-athletes.”

Frahm, a four-time first-team All-American, finished the 2026 season 21-6 in the circle with a 1.37 ERA over 189.2 innings while also hitting .403 with 20 home runs. As a pitcher, she finished 91-17 with a 1.29 ERA and 937 strikeouts.

Before her pregnancy news became public, Frahm opted not to play professionally this summer, though she remained on the AUSL’s list of provisional selections after its college draft. She could play in future seasons, as several active AUSL players also serve as college assistant coaches.

She is also part of the USA Softball Women’s National Team Pool and is expected to vie for a roster spot in the 2028 Olympics.
